articles.title: Delhi now has a lower fertility rate than the United States
articles.description: Low fertility rates are not just a feature of high-income countries.
paragraphs: In the opening of his 1968 book, The Population Bomb, Paul Ehrlich did little to hide his disdain for Delhi:

“People eating, people washing, people sleeping. People visiting, arguing, and screaming. People thrusting their hands through the taxi window, begging. People defecating and urinating. People clinging to buses. People herding animals. People, people, people, people. As we moved slowly through the mob, hand horns squawking, the dust, noise, heat, and cooking fires gave the scene a hellish aspect.”

Delhi’s population wasn’t even that large at the time: home to fewer than five million people, less than in London or Paris. 1 What Ehrlich was reacting to was probably poverty and lagging infrastructure, not overpopulation.
Since then, Delhi has changed a lot. It has gotten richer. Living standards have improved. Its population has grown. And most relevant to Ehrlich is that its fertility rates have plummeted.

Census-based estimates put its total fertility rate at around 4.5 children per woman in 1961. When Ehrlich was there in the mid-60s, it was probably still above 4. By the late 2000s it fell below two and dropped below the average fertility rate across the United States.

Note that this captures the expected number of children women will have based on the average birth rates of women at each age; it’s not the number women have already had by the end of their childbearing years.
Now, you might be thinking, this comparison is unfair. We’re comparing a city (where fertility rates are often lower than in rural areas) with the average across a whole country.
India’s fertility rate is around two; a bit above the US, but now below the replacement rate. Washington DC’s fertility rate is only slightly below Delhi’s, at 1.1.
What’s striking is how quickly rates have declined in India. They are rapidly converging with a country that is much, much richer per person.

This rapid decline in fertility rates across India has led to some demographic milestones that many wouldn’t believe. The number of babies being born peaked in 2001. The number of children peaked in 2004, too. 3
articles.lede: Low fertility rates are not just a feature of high-income countries.

articles.title: Daikin launches R32 retrofit solution for existing residential heat pump series
articles.description: The Japanese manufacturer claims its retrofit approach can reduce installation time by up to 22%, capital expenditure by up to 55%, and energy consumption by up to 16%. The new range comes in three capacity classes and incorporates integrated refrigerant safety technology.
paragraphs: Daikin has introduced new replacement technology for its R-32 (difluoromethane)-based Mini VRV 5 S-series heat pumps, enabling existing variable refrigerant volume (VRV) and variable refrigerant flow (VRF) systems using R-410A refrigerant to be upgraded to R-32 equipment while retaining suitable existing refrigerant piping and wiring.

According to Daikin, installation time can be shortened by up to 22% and capital expenditure reduced by up to 55% compared with a complete system replacement. The company also claims energy savings of up to 16% compared with equivalent R-410A systems.

The new Mini VRV 5 RXYSA-B replacement range will be available in three sizes – 4 HP, 5 HP, and 6 HP – and uses R-32 refrigerant, which has a global warming potential (GWP) of 675, approximately 68% lower than that of R-410A.

The existing Mini VRV 5 S-series platform offers nominal cooling capacities ranging from 12.1 kW to 15.5 kW and rated heating capacities of 8.4 kW to 10.7 kW, depending on the model. Maximum heating capacities reach 18 kW under specified test conditions.
The outdoor units feature a compact, single-fan design with a height of 869 mm, low-noise operation down to 39 dB(A), and support for total piping lengths of up to 300 meters.
The technical specifications refer to the existing RXYSA-A platform, as detailed performance data for the newly introduced RXYSA-B replacement models have not yet been confirmed.

The systems also incorporate Daikin’s Shîrudo refrigerant safety technology, designed to facilitate the use of mildly flammable R-32 refrigerant in occupied buildings. It includes integrated refrigerant leak detection sensors, audible and visual alarms, and automatic shut-off valves to limit refrigerant leakage.
According to Daikin, the factory-integrated safety measures facilitate compliance with IEC 60335-2-40 and simplify system design and installation, particularly in smaller indoor spaces.

articles.description: An 83 year old republican Congresswoman who mocked a child for supporting electric cars has lost her seat by 330 votes, after a recount.
paragraphs: An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, has lost her seat.

Christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.

Foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation, and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government. Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist and native of the district.

For the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek. Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).

Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher, and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).

Christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who said “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”
But then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram, where it gained traction.

Emily said Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”
I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.

Foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.
articles.lede: An 83 year old republican Congresswoman who mocked a child for supporting electric cars has lost her seat by 330 votes, after a recount.

articles.description: For decades, Briggs & Stratton has helped keep the lights on after the storm with its gas-powered generators. Now, the...
paragraphs: For decades, Briggs & Stratton has helped keep the lights on after the storm with its gas-powered generators. Now, the company is bringing that legacy to the electric age with a new 16 kWh backup battery designed to scale with your growing energy needs.

Briggs & Stratton partnered with Texas-based EG4 to offer an all American-branded solution for battery backup power solution last year, and its stackable SimpliPHI batteries helped make it easy to right-size home battery projects – but those batteries were limited in size, and limited in what they could actually offer. With the launch of the brand’s new, 16 kWh SimpliPHI battery, the company is ready to meet your energy needs … even if those needs take you up to 512 kWh. (!)

For context, the average US home uses about 865 kWh of energy per month, so a 512 kWh battery should theoretically keep your lights on for nearly 18 days after a storm – or provide basic power for your whole block for a weekend, at least!

“This launch represents a significant shift in our battery strategy,” explains Sequoya Cross, vice president of energy storage at Briggs & Stratton. “Our combined resources allow us to bring a competitively priced battery of the highest quality to energy storage installers.”

An onboard battery management system (BMS) and built-in Wi-Fi gateway help to streamline the system’s setup for installers, while the Briggs battery’s automatic inverter sensing technology supports closed-loop communication with Sol-Ark, Solis, EG4, Growatt, Megarevo, Victron, and other leading inverters. Other installer-friendly features include an IP65-rated enclosure allows for indoor or outdoor installation in either ground- or wall-mounted setups without requiring an additional cabinet, and an integrated circuit breaker that allows technicians to isolate the battery during servicing.

The battery itself is rated for 8,000 cycles at 90% depth of discharge, with a charge and discharge rate of 0.5C and an end-of-life capacity of 70%. Briggs & Stratton backs its new battery packs with a 12-year parts warranty that includes labor and travel costs, as well as a US-based tech support service.
The SimpliPHI 16 is available for pre-order now, though pricing was not mentioned in the original press release.

articles.description: The Illinois Clean Ports Program is putting $104 million behind efforts to help clean up its working waterfronts, funds earmarked...
paragraphs: Procurement is now underway for zero-emission vehicles, equipment, and supporting infrastructure at four sites across the state. Administered by the Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (Illinois EPA), Illinois’ Clean Ports Program aims to modernize operations at ports and waterfront facilities in Chicago, the Quad Cities, and southern Illinois’ river port districts.

“Illinois’ waterways are a competitive advantage for the state,” said Illinois Governor JB Pritzker, who was elected to a historic third term on 03NOV. “By modernizing port infrastructure, advancing zero-emission technology, and improving air quality, we are strengthening our economy while building a cleaner future for Illinois.”

Illinois’ Clean Ports Program isn’t just replacing diesel-powered equipment with electric alternatives – instead, the plan also includes Level 2 and DC fast charging, shore power and charging for electrified ships, and comprehensive grid upgrades designed to modernize existing port operations and support the deployment of new electric equipment.

The program takes a holistic approach to port electrification at Chicago’s Illinois International Port District (IIPD), treating energy generation, storage, and deployment as parts of a single connected system. On-site solar helps meet the port’s growing electricity needs while excess power is stored for peak hours, when grid electricity is most expensive. This setup reduces strain on the local grid, and acts as a hedge against rising energy costs.

For smaller public port districts, replacing aging equipment and upgrading electrical infrastructure can be an enormous financial undertaking. The Illinois Clean Ports Program helps make those investments possible, bringing cleaner, healthier, zero-emission technology within reach of terminal operators while preparing the state’s ports for a more competitive freight future.

articles.title: E-quipment highlight: Tadano rolls out 35-ton V320RC electric crane
articles.description: Developed by Japanese material handling giant Tadano, the 35-ton V320RC wheeled electric pick & carry crane has spent the last...
paragraphs: Developed by Japanese material handling giant Tadano, the 35-ton V320RC wheeled electric pick & carry crane has spent the last few months proving itself at NMG Italia’s job sites, where it’s been handling heavy loads in tight industrial spaces and improving efficiency by 50%. And now, you can buy one.

Developed in collaboration with NMG Italia, the V320RC electric crane has already proven its performance in the field with NMG and during precision setup operations at Marmomac, a trade show dedicated to the marble industry held each year in Verona.

“The ( Tadano) V320RC marks a real breakthrough in the pick & carry industry,” reads the official Tadano launch copy. “ Rather than an evolution of existing solutions, it introduces a new philosophy, with technologies and features capable of setting new benchmarks in the lifting market. Tadano and NMG Italia continue their collaboration in the field, turning real-world experience into new technological solutions to meet the most advanced demands of industrial lifting.”

The crane itself is a compact, battery-electric pick-and-carry machine with a maximum lifting capacity of 35 tonnes. Measuring just 5 m long, 2.15 m wide and 2.400 m tall (a meter is about a yard, guys – you got this), the V320RC is designed to bring heavy lifting capability into tight industrial spaces where larger cranes struggle to operate.

The new Tadano runs on a 120V, 1,120 Ah li-ion battery pack (that works out to ~134 kWh) and packs a gross vehicle weight of more than 31,150 kg (~34.5 short tones). That number includes 9,500 kg (~10 tons) of removable counterweights that make transport and handling easier for a wider range of customers. Under the hood, a new hydraulic system pairs a variable-displacement pump with what the company calls “an electro-hydraulic control valve” to improve precision and responsiveness while reducing energy consumption.

According to NMG Italia, all that baked-in tech V320RC give them 50% better productivity than competing electric cranes working under equivalent workloads, with enough battery capacity to support several days of operation between charges.

Rumor: Hyundai is getting ready to roll out an all-new, all-electric work truck
articles.description: The last time Hyundai announced a new work truck was 22 years ago, and the Hyundai Porter has proven itself...
paragraphs: The last time Hyundai announced a new work truck was 22 years ago, and the Hyundai Porter has proven itself as a dependable workhorse throughout Korea and Southeast Asia – but only the pyramids and the Chevy Express can last forever. Hyundai is reportedly getting ready to pull the wraps off an all-new Porter pickup. This time, it’s electric.

Distinct from the Piaggio-branded Porter pickup that’s already sold in Europe, the Hyundai Porter is a conceptually similar, work-focused vehicle with a dropside pickup “bed” trailing a box-like passenger cab and a serious, professional-grade payload capacity.

Carscoops recently published photos of a heavily camouflaged Hyundai Porter prototype last month, along with claims that Hyundai means to follow up the success of sister brand Kia’s multifunctional PV5 electric vans with a globally available electric version of the truck as early as next year. This week, the wraps came off, giving us our best look yet at what the truck might look like when it makes its official debut.

After feeding as many spy shots as I could into some AI models, we ended up with the images you see here. If they’re accurate, they show a commercial-ready EV that’s meant to attract new fleet buyers looking to ditch diesel in Western markets while serving as a direct, 1:1 replacement for domestic fleet operators already putting Porter pickups to work.

Those operators will probably feel a little safer behind the wheel of the new truck, too. Hyundai has worked a short hood and crash structure into the bodywork where a conventional “flat” cabover now sits – a move that seems to point both to a commitment to provide better front-end protection to the truck’s occupants and an intent to at least take an honest run at the Euro NCAP crash standards.

Beyond that, we don’t really know anything about the upcoming Korean pickup – but it’s a safe bet that the next-generation Porter will benefit from some of the technology that’s been baked into the Hyundai Motor Group’s E-GMP.S commercial vehicle platform that underpins the Kia PV vehicles. Those ship with 51.5 and 71.2 kWh battery options sending electrons to 120 kW (~160 hp) electric motors, and while that’s far from a guarantee, it’s not nothing, either.

That’s my take, anyway – what’s yours? Will the Hyundai Porter EV make its way to the West on an AWD version of the E-GMP.S platform, or will it remain a regional model running on one of the company’s hybrid platforms? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: Xiaomi’s 1,548 hp electric supercar is going global, starting in the UAE
articles.description: As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside...
paragraphs: As a red wave of Chinese-built electric vehicles breaks over Europe and Canada, Xiaomi is selling its electric cars outside of China for the first time ever – and its starting its push for global growth with the UAE in 2027.

Xiaomi is selling its electrified vehicles to buyers outside of China for first time this week, with the SU7 sedan, YU7 crossover, and Skynomad SUV now listed for sale throughout the United Arab Emirates (UAE). The company isn’t going it alone, however.

Xiomi is working local distributor Gargash Prime Automotive, rather than operating its own retail network, with Xiaomi CEO Lei Jun confirming that the company would officially enter Western car markets next year at the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen held 17NOV.

CarNewsChina reports that Gargash Prime Automotive is offering 13 variants across the Xiaomi SU7 sedan, YU7 SUV, and Skynomad extended-range electric SUV lineup, with retail prices starting at 169,900 AED ($~46,200 US) for the SU7 Standard and climbing all the way up to 375,900 AED ($~102,000 US) for the range-topping SU7 Ultra.

Not to lump a bunch of nations with their own rich heritage and car culture together, but it’s fair to say that drivers in the UAE, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait love their supercars – a nd the brand’s Xiaomi SU7 Ultra might be one of the most super of them all, thanks to fully 1,548 hp from three high-torque electric motors, the SU7 Ultra can sprint from 0-100 km/h (62 mph) in under two seconds on its way to a towering, 217 mph top speed.

It’s not just a straight-line speed machine, either. Xiaomi gave its go-fast flagship a serious track-focused makeover on its way to becomig the “Utlra,” complete with carbon-ceramic brakes, an aggressive ( if controversial) composite aero package, an enormous rear wing, and a chassis tuned to tackle the turns the Green Hell of the Nürburgring.

The first customer deliveries of the Xiaomi SU7 Standard and Ultra, YU7 Standard, and Skynomad N70 Pro models are scheduled for December of this year, with deliveries of the remaining variants scheduled for February 2027.

articles.title: Here are 7 great reasons rural drivers SHOULD embrace EVs in 2027
articles.description: America is full of rural communities that are miles away from major cities, and EVs offer rural drivers even more benefits!
paragraphs: America’s heartland is full of rural communities that are miles away from its major cities, both geographically and culturally – but that doesn’t mean these more sparsely populated regions can’t reap the benefits of electrification. In fact, EVs offer rural drivers even more benefits than they do to city-dwellers!

“An electric lifestyle would be a boon to our rural heartland,” wrote th e Union of Concerned Scientists’ Maria Cecilia Pinto de Moura. “Rural communities across the country have their own distinguishing characteristics, but certain shared characteristics such as driving distances, the type of vehicles driven, and socio-economics are factors which contribute to this larger potential to benefit from vehicle electrification.”

Pinto de Moura went on to outline five ways rural and country drivers could benefit from going electric – but that was in 2021, and a whole lot has changed in the nearly six years since. As such, I thought it was high time we revisit some of the reasons EVs are a great fit for rural lifestyles, see if we could uncover any new ones, and outline the reasons we think rural drivers should rush to embrace electric vehicles in the coming calendar year.

When you hear that line about, “the average American drives 30 to 40 miles a day,” remember that in towns like Wellington, Ohio, or Colfax, Washington, 30 miles is a grocery run. Each way. So when people trot out that old line about range anxiety, what rural drivers actually hear isn’t reassurance. It’s dismissal — a suggestion that they drive too far for an EV to work, when nothing could be further from the truth.

Country guys and gals love their pickups, and arguably the biggest difference between the EV market of 2021 and 2027 is that electric trucks and SUVs are no longer a novelty. There are now battery-powered options ready to haul, handle chores, head out camping, and tow a trailer.

With only about 45% of rural counties having access to DC fast charging, public charging still isn’t as visible as many first-time EV buyers might like, but it’s far better than it used to be — and improving fast. Still, that’s not the real EV advantage. Home charging is.

Unlike many apartment-dwelling urban drivers, most rural owners can charge right at home. More than 80% of rural households have a driveway or garage that are ideal for overnight Level 2 charging, and many already have a 240V outlet, keeping setup costs ( if there even are any) to a minimum.
Plug in before bed, wake up to a full battery every morning, and do it for pennies on the dollar, especially with off-peak rates.

If disaster strikes and you lose power, your EV could be more than just a way to get around. Many electric cars and trucks have the ability to power refrigerators, freezers, well pumps, lights, and other household essentials for days, either through onboard outlets or a dedicated vehicle-to-home (V2H) system that feeds electricity directly into your home’s electrical panel. Ford’s from-the-ashes F-150 Lightning and Tesla’s Cybertruck are already among the EVs making that capability a reality, and newer, more affordable electric trucks promise to bring V2H tech to even more households.
articles.lede: America is full of rural communities that are miles away from major cities, and EVs offer rural drivers even more benefits!

Tesla launches FSD v15, targets its biggest weaknesses, from signs to potholes
articles.description: Tesla's FSD v15 rollout targets sign reading, potholes and school-zone speeds, some of FSD's biggest weaknesses, plus an impressive new Reality View.
paragraphs: Tesla has started rolling out “Full Self-Driving” v15, and its list of improvements reads like a list of FSD’s biggest current weaknesses: sign detection, potholes, and speed handling in school zones.

Tesla also claims “25x better handling of safety critical cases” and is adding a new live visualization that looks seriously impressive. If the driving improvements are as real as the visuals, this is a big update.

Tesla announced the rollout on X this afternoon, and its Tesla Super Intelligence account followed up with the full release notes. The company didn’t say which vehicles get it first, but it has previously told investors that its AI4 (HW4) computer is enough to run v15.

Tesla’s main announcement also says FSD can now slow down for speed cameras, and it adds Bike Rack Mode, which allows FSD with a bike rack or a similar hitch accessory. Navigation learning only covers the start and end of trips for now; Tesla says later v15 releases will expand it to the entire route.

The new visualization is the flashiest part, and based on the video Tesla shared, it’s super impressive. The center screen shows a detailed, rendered version of the street around the car, far beyond the current FSD visualization.

Tesla calls it “Reality View” in its announcement and “Tesla Augmented Reality” in the release notes. The notes say it replaces all the separate model signals with a single end-to-end visualization that uses less compute, and Tesla says it lets the driver “see & control what FSD is planning to do.” If that works as advertised, it could make supervising the system a lot easier.
What stands out more is where Tesla is focusing. Almost every driving improvement in the release notes targets an area where FSD struggles today.

Signs are a big one. In a test published in September, Brussels nonprofit Johanna.be found that FSD exceeded the limit in 55% of the 30 km/h zones it drove through, averaging 44 km/h. In most of those zones, the car’s screen showed a 50 km/h limit. It didn’t read the sign.
Potholes are another. In August, Musk said pothole avoidance was “coming soon”, something he had already promised back in 2019. Today, FSD still drives straight through them.

School zones are on the list too. NHTSA is reviewing a petition claiming Tesla’s Robotaxis speed through active school zones, on top of an investigation it opened in October 2025 into FSD traffic-law violations like running red lights. Slowing for speed cameras fits the same theme, though it also suggests Tesla is fine with FSD going over the limit when there’s no camera around.
articles.lede: Tesla's FSD v15 rollout targets sign reading, potholes and school-zone speeds, some of FSD's biggest weaknesses, plus an impressive new Reality View.

articles.title: How much does charging an EV really cost? This Redditor says $7 per month
articles.description: One of the most common questions asked by first-time EV buyers is about the cost of electricity. Whether they plan...
paragraphs: Whether we’re talking gasoline, diesel, or electricity, one driver’s fuel costs can look dramatically different from another’s. How far they drive, how often, and under what conditions can matter just as much as what they drive. And while EVs may offer the greatest benefits to rural drivers covering long distances, a Redditor going by Suitable-Truth-350 took a different approach, moving into a highly walkable city for the express purpose of driving as little as possible.

“My wife and I recently retired and moved from a car dependent, rural/suburban area to a large, walkable city with good light rail. Our goal was to drive as little as possible,” write Suitable-Truth-350. “We took delivery of an Ioniq5 in August. We still have a daily walking life, but we use the car to see friends in the country, shop or travel around the greater Chicagoland area. After 2 months, we finally charged it.”

“Driving the car is a pleasure,” they continue. “The pickup and smooth operation so different from our last ICE vehicle. First impression, we love the car and could never imagine going back to (a gasoline-powered car).”

I’ve been saying it for years: drive an EV for a week and whatever range anxiety you might experience will disappear. And, while it seems like Suitable-Truth-350 didn’t have much range anxiety to begin with, it’s worth noting here that their situation isn’t that rare.

In their most recent national survey, AAA found that the average US driver covered less than 29 miles per day, with the vast majority weekly commuting totals falling well within the range of even the most affordable used EVs.
The same survey found that just 30% of Americans reported taking at least one road trip the previous summer, with an average one-way trip length of ~235 miles.

That 235 mile trip might be too much for a car like the Fiat 500e, but even that car – the new EV with the shortest EPA-estimated range you can buy in the US – can make a 235 mile trip with a single 30-minute stop to charge. And in 2026 and 2027, they’re sure to find plenty of places to charge, thanks to a public charging network that’s newer, faster, and far more built out than they probably think, with more fast-charging locations opening every week and modern charging speeds that make longer stops the exception instead of the norm.
🤔 so if you drive very little, you will have to charge very little. I’m not sure how this straightforward logic is newsworthy.

articles.title: Tesla Cybertruck’s already impressive turning radius gets even tighter
articles.description: Tesla is rolling out an update that tightens the Cybertruck turning radius, but only on 2027 trucks, just months before production ends.
paragraphs: Tesla is rolling out an update that makes the Cybertruck turn even tighter, improving on what was already one of the best turning radiuses you can get in a full-size pickup.
But there’s a catch. It only works on 2027 model year Cybertrucks, and Tesla plans to stop building the truck by the end of next summer.

Tesla’s official Cybertruck account posted a short drone video early Saturday showing a truck doing circles in a parking lot, with a “before” and “after” comparison of its turning path. “Even tighter turns now rolling out to new Cybertrucks,” the account wrote.
In a follow-up post, Tesla said the improvement requires software version 2026.44 or newer and “only applies to model year 2027 Cybertrucks.”
Tesla didn’t share a new turning circle figure. In the video, the “after” circle is visibly smaller than the “before” one by what looks to be at least a foot.

The Cybertruck’s maneuverability comes from its rear-wheel steering paired with steer-by-wire. At low speeds, the rear wheels turn opposite to the fronts, which shrinks the space the truck needs to make a U-turn. We’ve been tracking the Cybertruck’s four-wheel steering since the prototype days, when Tesla was showing it off in parking garages.

Even before this update, the results were impressive. Tesla’s owner’s manual lists the Cybertruck’s curb-to-curb turning circle at about 43.5 ft (13.25 m). That beats the Ford F-150 Lightning at roughly 47.8 ft and the Rivian R1T at 44.9 ft, and it’s within about 4 ft of a Model Y. Not bad for a 6,600-lb truck that’s nearly 19 feet long.

And Tesla always said there was more to come. At launch, the rear wheels turned only about 3 degrees. In early 2024, a Tesla engineer said a software update would push that to 10 degrees, and Elon Musk said the company had improvements in the works to “tighten the turning circle significantly.”

Tesla hasn’t said whether this update delivers the full 10 degrees, or why it’s limited to 2027 trucks. If it comes down to hardware, owners of earlier Cybertrucks who were counting on this as an over-the-air upgrade are out of luck.

Credit where it’s due. The turning circle is one of the best things about the Cybertruck, and anyone who has driven one knows it. Steer-by-wire combined with rear-wheel steering is real engineering, and other vehicles are just starting to get that combo a couple years after Cybertruck had it. Making it even better is a nice update.
articles.lede: Tesla is rolling out an update that tightens the Cybertruck turning radius, but only on 2027 trucks, just months before production ends.

articles.title: Toyota just built a tiny folding electric bike to fit in your trunk
articles.description: Toyota is getting into electric bikes. Well, sort of. The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny...
paragraphs: The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation.

And when Toyota says compact, it means it. The little electric ride can reportedly fold up in around 30 seconds and become small enough to fit inside the trunk of the brand’s GR86 sports car. Think of it like Toyota’s take on the Motocompacto.

The BKE Concept was unveiled as part of the newly revived Scion by Toyota brand, which the company is positioning less as the return of the quirky youth-oriented car brand many Americans remember and more as a sort of experimental mobility laboratory.

Toyota calls the new Scion a “freedom lab” where the company can explore vehicles and mobility concepts that don’t necessarily fit neatly into its conventional automotive lineup. Alongside the BKE, Toyota showed its KEI-01 ultra-compact utility truck and a hybrid side-by-side.
But perhaps unsurprisingly for me, it’s the tiny electric two-wheeler that caught my attention.

And I should point out here that while Toyota refers to it as an “electric bike” in its own brand literature, the lack of pedals means that the cute little two-wheeler is not going to qualify as an electric bicycle in Europe or North America. The moniker means it merely slots into the broader electric bike category that encompasses everything from electric bicycles to scooters and motorcycles. In essence, the BKE is more or less a small seated e-scooter, sometimes referred to as a “no-ped”.
Despite looking like the kind of concept vehicle that might have been whipped up for an auto show, Toyota says the BKE has actually been under development for several years.
A small team of chassis and electrical engineers has reportedly been testing and refining the design based on real-world use and feedback.
The basic idea came from a fairly simple question: How could Toyota make short-distance mobility easier and integrate it more seamlessly into everyday life?
The result is essentially a secondary vehicle designed to travel inside your primary vehicle.
articles.lede: The Japanese automotive giant has unveiled the BKE Concept, a tiny folding electric two-wheeler designed to serve as a compact companion vehicle for short trips, outdoor adventures, and last-mile transportation.

E-quipment highlight: Mantsinen 200 material handler has tank treads
articles.description: Are you a port or rail terminal operator looking for a new electric material handler that can move serious cargo...
paragraphs: Are you a port or rail terminal operator looking for a new electric material handler that can move serious cargo without sacrificing maneuverability? Do you wish it had tank treads? If that’s you, the Mantsinen 200 might be just the thing.

Designed to handle demanding port and rail terminal operations, the Finnish-built Matsinen 200 material handler combines impressive reach and lifting capacity with the ability to move around a worksite on its own tracks. And, yes: I said tracks.

By far the most fun feature of the Mantsinen 200 is the fact that it looks like a rejected concept for a ROBOTIX dinosaur set and/or something He-Man would use to run over Trap Jaw. And while, yes – most big material handlers have similar form factors, there’s something about the 200 that really sells the whole Dragon Walker vibe.

The Mantsinen 200 is powered by a 380 kW (~510 hp) grid-connected electric motor running at 1,800 rpm. Power comes from a 460V electrical connection as standard, with other voltage options available to suit local site requirements.

Mantsinen says its electrically powered machines deliver the same performance as their diesel counterparts, while eliminating exhaust emissions at the machine and reducing operating noise, energy consumption and maintenance costs. Power is delivered through a load-sensing hydraulic system featuring four variable-displacement piston pumps and a separate closed-loop swing circuit.

Mantsinen also fits the 200 with its proprietary HybriLift energy-recovery system. HybriLift works a lot like regenerative braking by capturing potential energy as the main boom is lowered, but instead of storing that energy as electricity in a battery, the material handler stores it in hydraulic accumulators for reuse during the next lift. The company claims HybriLift improves the big machine’s energy efficiency by up to 50%, effectively giving the machine an additional 300 (ish) hp of lifting assistance at average lifting speed.

And, while the machine normally draws power from the grid, operators aren’t necessarily tethered to an outlet. Mantsinen offers an optional PowerPack that allows the machine to disconnect from its main power supply and still travel around the worksite, with some basic hydraulic systems still functional. The PowerPack is currently diesel-powered, but a battery-backed version isn’t out of the question. It’s a useful bit of flexibility for terminal operators who want the benefits of electric material handling without giving up the ability to reposition the machine when a fixed electrical connection isn’t available.
What do you guys think – is this big material handler the thing you need for your logging or scrapyard, or are you holding out for something even bigger? Let us know in the comments.

articles.title: I ride e-bikes for a living. This is the real gear I actually use
articles.description: I’m in the somewhat unusual position of basically riding electric bicycles for a living. I’ve been working with e-bikes for...
paragraphs: I’m in the somewhat unusual position of basically riding electric bicycles for a living. I’ve been working with e-bikes for nearly two decades, professionally covering the e-bike industry for most of that time, testing hundreds of different models and traveling around the world to ride new e-bikes in some pretty incredible places. Yeah, it’s a tough job – but someone’s got to suffer it.

Of course I don’t just ride e-bikes for work. I ride them recreationally. I ride them for exercise. I ride them for transportation. My family doesn’t even own a car, meaning two wheels handle the vast majority of our transportation.
In other words: I talk the talk and I walk the walk. Or perhaps more accurately, I ride the ride.

And while most of the time all you really need for a good ride is an e-bike and a direction to go in, there are a handful of pieces of gear that I’ve come to rely on over the years. Some keep me safer. Some keep my bikes out of the hands of thieves. Some make rides more comfortable or convenient. And some are just neat little things that I’ve discovered along the way.

If you own nice e-bikes, you’re eventually going to spend a lot of time thinking about locks. Your lock may even be your most important accessory. Or perhaps I should say “accessories”, because the best way to ensure your e-bike is still there when you get back is to use more than one solid lock.
My go-to options that I grab basically every day for the last couple of years have been Seatylock’s FoldyLock Forever folding lock and Mason 220 U-lock.

For reference, the Foldylock Forever is the world’s strongest folding lock. That’s not just their marketing speak, but rather it’s confirmed by independent testing and certification. It’s the only folding lock in the world to achieve an ART 3-star security rating awarded by the Stichting ART Foundation, an independent Dutch organization that tests and certifies anti-theft locks. It earned that certification three years ago, and no other folding lock has been able to reach that level yet. The only higher ratings ART gives are for locks rated for motorcycles.
Personally, I like folding locks because they pack relatively neatly on the bike while still giving me enough flexibility to work around different racks and poles, or even larger things like trees.

The FoldyLock Forever is the one I reach for when I want serious security matched with more flexibility, while the Mason 220 gives me another beefy option when I know a U-lock will fit what I’m locking to.

The Mason is great as a strong U-lock, but I also like how large it is, letting me lock to wider poles and also a tad bit farther from the pole itself, leaving room for pannier bags and other things that get in the way. Amazingly, it’s also one of the few U-locks I have that can fit over the beefy battery-filled downtube on most of my e-bikes.
articles.lede: I’m in the somewhat unusual position of basically riding electric bicycles for a living.

Electric cars are finally mainstream in GTA 6, and Vice City is full of them
articles.description: GTA 6 electric vehicles are everywhere in Vice City: Tesla and Porsche lookalikes, ReVolt America chargers, even ICEd stalls. Here's how far GTA EVs came.
paragraphs: Electric vehicles have finally gone mainstream in Grand Theft Auto. In GTA 6, EVs are just part of everyday traffic in Vice City, from Tesla and Porsche lookalikes to a parody of Electrify America’s charging network.
It’s a big change for a series that spent over a decade treating EVs as a Tesla joke. After a few days of playing, I’d say Rockstar nailed the vibe.
I’ve been playing GTA 6 since it launched on Thursday, partly for fun and partly because I wanted to see how Rockstar would handle EVs this time. The answer: a lot better than I expected.
The game starts you in the Keys, Rockstar’s take on the Florida Keys, and it’s a rougher part of Leonida. Lots of older cars and beaters, and you won’t see many EVs.

That changes as you head north to Vice City, the game’s version of Miami. The closer you get, the more electric cars show up in traffic, and the more charging stations you pass. By the time you’re in the city, EVs are just normal cars.
That’s pretty much how EV adoption looks in the real world, concentrated in big, wealthier metro areas while rural areas lag behind.

That last one got me. Gas cars blocking chargers has been a complaint for as long as public charging has existed, and we’ve covered EV owners blocking a gas station in protest over ICEing. Rockstar recreating it tells me someone at the studio has actually tried to charge an EV in public. Probably even in Florida, which they tried to recreate here.
GTA 6 is the first mainline GTA where energy matters. Gas cars burn fuel and need a pump, and EVs have a battery level and need a plug.
Rockstar could have used that to make EVs a pain. It didn’t. In my testing, the EVs have about the same range as the gas cars, charge just as fast as a fill-up, and cost the same or less to top up.

Kotaku’s range test backs that up. On the same highway loop, a Tesla Model 3 lookalike lasted 20 minutes and 23 seconds on a charge, longer than the Banshee sports car at 18 minutes and 31 seconds, and not far off an old pickup at 29 minutes and 8 seconds. Crossing the whole map by highway takes under 15 minutes, according to Kotaku.
articles.lede: GTA 6 electric vehicles are everywhere in Vice City: Tesla and Porsche lookalikes, ReVolt America chargers, even ICEd stalls. Here's how far GTA EVs came.

articles.title: Elon Musk freezes at awkward Tesla Argentina launch: ‘I don’t know what to say’
articles.description: Elon Musk joined Tesla's Argentina launch with Milei by video and froze: 'I don't really know what I want to say.' The Model 3 starts at $40,990.
paragraphs: Tesla officially launched in Argentina on Friday with President Javier Milei on stage in Buenos Aires, and Elon Musk joined by video from his plane to welcome the brand’s newest market. It didn’t go well.

Musk got through one line about Tesla before stalling out: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.” The call ended about two minutes in, without any real pitch for the Model 3 or Model Y that Tesla had just put on sale.

The launch took place at Arenas Studio in Buenos Aires’ La Boca neighborhood. Milei spoke for less than eight minutes, then the host asked the room to welcome “our next guest,” and Musk popped up on the giant screen from what looked like an airplane cabin. Milei burst out laughing and bounced on his feet.
Musk started fine: “Hello, Argentina. Well, here we are. It’s a joy to share Tesla with all of you and to establish ourselves there.”

Then he started glancing off to each side. “Actually, I don’t really know what to say, other than thank you for this welcome to Tesla in Argentina,” he said. He briefly mentioned a charging network with state-owned oil company YPF, thanked the audience again, and then: “Sorry, I don’t really know what I want to say.”
Milei tried to save it. Back on stage, he told the crowd that “those who do a lot, talk little,” and called Musk “the Leonardo da Vinci of the 21st century.”
The clip is now spreading fast in Argentina, with one post of the video racking up over 1.1 million views overnight.
Tesla opened online orders on Friday for five versions of the Model 3 and Model Y, all imported from Gigafactory Shanghai. Here are the list prices, VAT included:

Argentina is Tesla’s fourth direct-sales market in South America after Chile, Colombia, and Uruguay, which launched in July. Tesla is late to the party, though. BYD already leads Argentina’s EV market after Milei’s government cut import taxes on electric vehicles.
What I really found awkward was hearing Musk stating " I'm not MAGA, I'm not sure what MAGA means " in his interview with CNBC.
articles.lede: Elon Musk joined Tesla's Argentina launch with Milei by video and froze: 'I don't really know what I want to say.' The Model 3 starts at $40,990.

CATL, BYD, ACWA among co-initiators of storage alliance unveiled at COP31
articles.description: An international energy storage cooperation initiative backed by 27 companies and institutions has been formally launched at the UN climate conference in Turkey.
paragraphs: The Global Energy Storage Alliance, known as GESA, was launched on Nov. 13 at the China Pavilion during COP31 in Antalya, Turkey, bringing together 27 co-initiating organizations spanning battery manufacturers, power utilities, state-owned enterprises, and research institutions from China and several other countries.

The three founding organizations are the China Energy Storage Alliance, the China Renewable Energy Engineering Institute, and China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage Co. The co-initiator list includes battery and system manufacturers such as CATL, BYD Energy Storage, EVE Energy, Hithium, and Sungrow, alongside state-owned energy groups including CGN Energy International and POWERCHINA International. Saudi Arabian utility developer ACWA Power is among the international co-initiators. Seven organizations — including the Long Duration Energy Storage Council, the International Hydropower Association, Energy Storage Europe, and the World Resources Institute are listed as interested in exploring participation in GESA.

The launch event was attended by Liu Zhenmin, China’s Special Envoy for Climate Change; Francesco La Camera, Director-General of the International Renewable Energy Agency; Armida Salsiah Alisjahbana, UN Under-Secretary-General and Executive Secretary of ESCAP; and Xiong Minfeng, Deputy Director-General of the International Cooperation Department at China’s National Energy Administration.

GESA’s founding declaration outlines six areas of focus: facilitating international dialogue, building a global storage project and standards database, supporting research and technology deployment, improving market mechanisms, strengthening supply chains and trade, and mobilizing investment for projects in developing economies. The initiative describes itself as open, technology-neutral, and market-oriented, and states it will respect different national regulatory models.

Speaking at the launch, Sun Liqun, Deputy General Manager of China Southern Power Grid Energy Storage, identified three structural barriers the initiative aims to address: inadequate market mechanisms for valuing both short- and long-duration storage, fragmented technical standards and regulatory frameworks across countries, and financing and development barriers in emerging economies. These are widely recognized constraints on storage deployment. However, how the degree to which a voluntary industry alliance can move them will depend on the engagement it obtains beyond the launch.

Beyond industry coordination, the alliance carries weight in the UN-led climate process. Storage underpins the global push to triple renewable capacity by 2030, and GESA’s focus on technical assistance, capacity building and de-risked financing for developing economies speaks directly to the Paris Agreement’s call for an equitable transition. By channeling South-South cooperation toward emerging markets in Southeast Asia, the Middle East and Latin America, where financing costs remain the biggest obstacle to deployment, the initiative could help narrow the energy access gap between developed and developing countries.
articles.lede: An international energy storage cooperation initiative backed by 27 companies and institutions has been formally launched at the UN climate conference in Turkey.

articles.title: Celebrating men, challenging stereotypes, building a stronger energy future together
articles.description: On International Men's Day, and as Movember raises awareness of men's health and wellbeing, Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) and Solar+ Leaders celebrate the men across the solar and wider energy transition industries who are helping build a more inclusive future. Carmen Madrid, Founder of both initiatives, draws on perspectives shared throughout the network's pv magazine series to reflect on why gender equality is not about women versus men, but about creating workplaces where everyone can thrive, lead authentically and contribute their full potential to the energy transition.
paragraphs: Someone once asked me why I had decided to create a women’s network in the solar industry. My answer was simple: “Because our industry is full of good men who already want to change the world, and I couldn’t think of better ground on which to build a network that could help us change it together.”

On International Men’s Day, Women in Solar+ Europe (WiSEu) wants to celebrate the men across our solar, energy storage and wider energy transition industries. The men who recognise talent beyond gender, challenge stereotypes, encourage others to grow and understand that creating a more inclusive industry is a shared responsibility. Many do so without recognition, through everyday decisions that shape careers, workplaces and opportunities for others.

Our industry has something extraordinary in common: a purpose that goes far beyond individual careers or commercial success. We are working towards a more sustainable, secure and resilient energy future. And that shared ambition gives us powerful common ground to rethink not only how we produce energy, but how we work together.

Gender equality is sometimes presented as a competition between women and men, as though creating opportunities for one group necessarily means taking something away from another. Yet the experiences shared throughout our Women in Solar+ Europe series suggest a different reality. Inclusion is about removing limitations, not creating new ones, and allowing people to contribute according to their abilities rather than expectations attached to their gender.

Antonio Arruebo, Senior Market Analyst at SolarPower Europe, captured this perspective in our previous reflections on gender equality: “Gender equality liberates everyone.” His message challenges us to recognise that stereotypes restrict men too, particularly when leadership is associated with authority, certainty or emotional restraint. Creating more inclusive workplaces also creates space for men to lead differently, express vulnerability and develop their own potential.

This is an important conversation for an industry that needs increasingly diverse capabilities. Technical expertise remains essential, but so do empathy, collaboration, adaptability and the ability to bring people together around complex challenges. None of these qualities belongs exclusively to one gender.

Progress also requires the courage to acknowledge that none of us is free from bias. We all develop assumptions through our upbringing, education and professional experiences. What matters is whether we are willing to recognise them and reconsider how they influence our decisions.

Emiliano Bellini, News Director at pv magazine, explored this in his contribution to our series, encouraging open conversations and greater tolerance for mistakes when addressing unconscious bias. His message was clear: “We must free our thinking and allow room for mistakes.”

This is particularly relevant when engaging more men in conversations about inclusion. Fear of saying the wrong thing should not prevent participation. We need environments where people can ask questions, disagree respectfully, learn from different perspectives and evolve together. Inclusion cannot flourish if conversations become another space where people feel judged rather than encouraged to grow.

Unigrid looks to fill gaps in lithium-ion storage with effective sodium-ion alternatives
articles.description: CEO Darren Tan says sodium-ion batteries can compete on safety, performance and price in key market segments.
paragraphs: San Diego-based Unigrid is hoping to make sodium-ion a household name. The company’s development team grew out of research centered on the University of California, San Diego, with the goal of providing battery storage technology to serve the markets where lithium-ion is not as suitable.
Unigrid CEO Darren Tan told pv magazine USA that while there are many categories in which lithium ion does well, sodium-ion battery chemistries have advantages in important market segments.

“You’ve got better safety,” Tan said, indicating sodium-ion chemistries are not flammable. “You’ve got extremely long cycle and calendar life. Sodium just doesn’t die. Also, sodium chemistries have great thermal tolerance; they don’t care how hot it is in summer or how cold it is winter. The biggest disadvantage of the batteries is that they are heavier and take up a little more space.”

The company says its 48V Na+ Casa series batteries, which are positioned for commercial and residential storage, have a discharge temperature range of about -100°F to +140°F and will charge down to about -68°F. They are UN38.3 certified and tested to UL 9540A standards at the cell level. The fire resistance of sodium-ion chemistries makes the suitable for deployment indoors, such as in hospitals or multi-unit housing.
At the same time, residential and commercial storage remains dominated by lithium-ion battery makers that are well ensconced with recognized brands with ever-increasing track records.
While there are examples of alternate chemistries and technologies, such as flow batteries, making inroads in the market, these suppliers face an uphill climb.

It is tempting, Tan says, to lump battery storage into a single category, but in reality, it is many, many vertical market segments. Lithium-ion chemistries, he concedes, have come to dominate the midrange endurance needs, from two to about six hours. Moreover, they are favored in many applications, from portable devices, to vehicles to grid-connected BESS. One aspect of this dominance is that suppliers and developers using them have ready access to financing.

Lithium-ion solutions are bankable, even standard, which industry analysts have pointed out may deter the development and deployment of more appropriate technologies in key markets. At the same time, Tan says sodium-ion is starting to get its strides in certain sectors, for example the short duration space.

For many years, there was no real demand to fill the gap between very short-duration – minutes or even seconds – applications provided by supercapacitors and the mid-range provided by batteries. However, Tan says, the advent of AI began producing strains on the grid, with demand moving from traditional arbitrage into things like ancillary services.

“You’ve got to service things like demand response,” Tan said. “You’ve got to provide capacity for uninterruptible loads; you’ve got to provide short demand charges based on load shifting. And lithium-ion is not great for that kind of high-power quick response. It also doesn’t like multiple cycles. Short-duration storage in data centers may need to cycle 10, 20 times a day, especially if you’re looking at an AI model training context.”
articles.lede: CEO Darren Tan says sodium-ion batteries can compete on safety, performance and price in key market segments.

articles.title: Spain approves new data center rules requiring 80% renewable electricity
articles.description: The new framework introduces energy and water efficiency standards, renewable electricity procurement obligations, and grid flexibility requirements for data centers. A €17.14 billion transmission network plan will support 47.4 GW of new electricity demand through 2030.
paragraphs: The Spanish government approved a royal decree on Nov. 20 establishing energy sustainability, environmental, resilience and digital sovereignty requirements for data centers. The Council of Ministers also approved the country’s electricity transmission network development plan through 2030, which was presented last week.
Third Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Ecological Transition Sara Aagesen announced the measures following the cabinet meeting.

The regulation comes amid rapid growth in electricity demand from data centers and artificial intelligence infrastructure. According to Aagesen, data center projects have secured grid access permits for 15 GW of capacity, including 6 GW on the transmission network and 9 GW on distribution networks. This represents nearly 40% of Spain’s peak electricity demand, while a further 20 GW of capacity is awaiting grid access.
These figures significantly exceed the projections in Spain’s 2024 Artificial Intelligence Strategy, which anticipated less than 4 GW of data center electricity demand by 2030.

The government had already raised concerns about the potential impact of large-scale data center development on electricity demand, grid capacity and renewable energy deployment. In August, it proposed requiring data centers to source at least 80% of their electricity from additional renewable generation.
The approved decree introduces several changes to the initial proposal published in August, including a higher capacity threshold for the main requirements.

The revised framework targets data centers with grid access capacity of at least 10 MW, up from the 1 MW threshold initially proposed. It establishes requirements covering renewable electricity procurement, energy and water efficiency, grid flexibility, resilience and digital sovereignty.

Data centers must demonstrate that at least 80% of their annual electricity consumption is covered by on-site renewable generation or long-term power purchase agreements (PPAs) with new renewable energy facilities.

The decree also introduces hourly matching requirements between electricity consumption and renewable generation, with a phased implementation period extending to 2032. Eligible facilities can follow a transitional compliance pathway, subject to conditions including participation in demand reduction mechanisms.

The regulation requires qualifying facilities to meet class A standards under the European classification systems for power usage effectiveness (PUE) and water usage effectiveness (WUE). Energy efficiency requirements will also take account of regional climatic conditions.
articles.lede: The new framework introduces energy and water efficiency standards, renewable electricity procurement obligations, and grid flexibility requirements for data centers.

articles.title: Battery patents: Solid-state filings surpass lithium-ion to hit record high
articles.description: Global solid-state battery patent filings hit a record 2,230 in 2024, up 16%, with South Korea overtaking Japan, driven by Samsung SDI’s rapid growth. Meanwhile, lithium-ion patent filings fell nearly 15% to 2,092, while sodium-ion filings dropped 29%, signaling a shift in battery innovation toward solid-state technologies.
paragraphs: Global patent filings for solid-state batteries reached a record 2,230 in 2024, up 16% from 2023. That’s according to the sixth annual Inside Green Innovation: Progress Report by intellectual property firm Appleyard Lees, which tracks patent filings across domains including food, such as cultivated meat, recycling, and fusion energy.

In contrast, lithium-ion battery patents across chemistries and applications fell nearly 15% to 2,092, with the data clerly showing consecutive years of declines. The report tracks complete public patent data through December 31, 2024, given delays across regions in visibility of applications.

South Korea overtook Japan to lead global solid-state filings in 2024, posting 873 applications compared to Japan’s 605. Japan had held the top spot every year through 2023, but South Korea’s nearly 50% year-on-year surge, driven largely by Samsung SDI, shifted the balance. Samsung SDI nearly doubled its solid-state filings from 165 to 325, more than twice Toyota’s combined total of 144.

China ranked third in solid-state priority filings with 217, more than doubling its output since 2022, while Europe reached a record 177 filings. South Korea also maintained the lead in conventional lithium-ion filings, which nearly doubled from 441 in 2020 to 833 in 2024.

Chris Mason, Partner at Appleyard Lees, said solid-state electrolytes showed the strongest growth in the data, while lithium-ion technologies “appear to be consolidating, with filing numbers decreasing for a second consecutive year.”
In part, this reflections the maturing and commercialized supply chain around LFP cells for stationary energy storage. Patent volume is generally a lagging indicator of R&D spend.

Meanwhile, sodium-ion patent activity cooled after a record 2023, dropping 29% from 555 filings to 392, though still outpacing any year prior to 2022. European organizations filed a record 76 sodium-ion patents in 2024, taking second place behind China.
Appleyard Lees said “flow battery filings remain on a plateau” that began in 2016, even as grid-scale storage is deployed at record rates.
Though not strictly related to energy storage, the annual coverage of fusion energy always reveals interesting trends in technology development. The report says, quote:
“Fusion is becoming a platform technology sector, as much as an energy sector, generating intellectual property with relevance far beyond future fusion power plants.
articles.lede: Global solid-state battery patent filings hit a record 2,230 in 2024, up 16%, with South Korea overtaking Japan, driven by Samsung SDI’s rapid growth.

Why tribal rights have become key to the energy permitting debate
articles.description: Climate advocates have debated the bill’s emissions impact. In the Senate, tribal sovereignty proved to be the bigger sticking point.
paragraphs: For months, the climate world and the broader Democratic coalition have argued over whether the sweeping bipartisan permitting reform bill will be good or bad for the energy transition. But inside the Senate, which just passed the legislation by a 62 – 33 vote, concerns about tribal sovereignty overshadowed the debate over emissions — and now are likely to influence negotiations in the House, too.

While tribal nations have sovereignty over development within their reservation boundaries, any development on sacred sites and cultural resources beyond those boundaries is subject to a special review under the 1966 National Historic Preservation Act. That law requires federal agencies to consult with tribes, but not to win their consent.

Large-scale energy projects, including the 550 -mile SunZia transmission line that carries wind power from New Mexico to Arizona and California, have previously drawn pushback from tribes despite the federal government engaging in these NHPA reviews. Some influential tribal organizations believe that the proposed changes to the NHPA under the permitting bill would infringe on their sovereignty — and water down the already imperfect government-to-government consultation process.

“ Tribes are sovereign, and that does mean that they need to be able to have a meaningful say in the pretty rare instances where a development might impact an important historical or cultural site that is not on their reservation lands,” said Julian Brave NoiseCat, a member of the Canim Lake Band Tsq̓éscen of the Secwépemc Nation in British Columbia as well as an author and Oscar-nominated filmmaker who previously worked at the climate group 350 .org.

These concerns took center stage as the Senate debated the bill, which analysts widely expect would benefit both clean energy and fossil fuels. Several large environmental groups have come out against the legislation over fears that it will increase planet-warming emissions, but the clean energy industry and some decarbonization advocates see the changes as essential for the energy transition.

In the end, the bill’s initial NHPA language was amended in response to concerns over sections that weakened tribal consultation and allowed for Interior Department oversight of Tribal Historic Preservation Offices. A bipartisan amendment that would have further strengthened tribal consultation on permitting, negotiated by Senate Indian Affairs Committee Chair Sen. Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) and Vice Chair Sen. Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), failed following a last-ditch attempt by Sen. Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) to scuttle the bill due to a host of criticisms.
As of Friday, many tribal organizations, including the National Congress of American Indians and the National Association of Tribal Historic Preservation Officers, remain opposed to the bill.

Tribal issues are likely to loom large over the debate in the House, too, where the bill will presumably face opposition from progressive Democrats who take issue with its environmental rollbacks. But the bill’s supporters are also pressuring representatives to act before the clock runs out on this session of Congress, making the odds of passing any substantive amendments — like the ones proposed in the Senate — slim.
articles.lede: Climate advocates have debated the bill’s emissions impact. In the Senate, tribal sovereignty proved to be the bigger sticking point.

Why load growth has changed how AES builds
articles.description: As demand surges, FERC has approved the IPP and utility company’s take-private deal with BlackRock and EQT.
paragraphs: Juan Ignacio Rubiolo has seen everything in energy change around him over the last few years. But at AES, his company of 25 years, the strategy transformed long before the data center boom.

Rubiolo, who was named chief operating officer of AES earlier this year, joined the company when it was primarily a fossil fuel power producer; coal made up a large chunk of the company’s business as recently as a decade ago. But in 2022, AES announced plans to exit coal by 2025 (though it has since moved the target to 2027; a major Puerto Rico plant is a notable holdout, allowed to operate until 2032). And in the years since, it added around three gigawatts of renewables and storage to its mix annually.

But demand has surged so much in the last few years that it needed to bring in new sources of capital to meet it — and change its entire make-up as a result. That’s true for both its IPP arm, which is roughly 70% of the company, and its utility arm, roughly 30% of the company. AES owns two Midwest utilities, AES Ohio and Indiana, in addition to several distribution utilities in El Salvador.

This week, AES’ acquisition by BlackRock and EQT got its final FERC approval, in what will be one of the largest ever utility take-private deals. This means AES will become a private company after 35 years trading on public markets.

As Ben Hertz-Shargel, global head of grid edge at Wood Mackenzie, told Latitude Media in March, the deal demonstrates that “utilities are a growth story” — and that many utilities and power producers need to invest heavily to meet demand, in some cases with external help.

“We still keep the same North Star,” Rubiolo told Latitude Media as the company awaited approval for the merger. The vast majority of its investments are in renewables, and its largest customer segments haven’t shifted: Hyperscalers dominate in the U.S., and mining companies in Latin America.

But there’s a shift in how the company is meeting the new demands of those customers, said Rubiolo, because of the need for speed. Hyperscalers want the same thing they’ve always wanted — new and ideally clean capacity — but far more and faster than ever before. AES said in February that the company has nearly 12 GW of energy contracted with data center customers.
As a result, the company is exploring more types of generation than ever before, including fuel cells and natural gas, and in the longer term, advanced geothermal and small modular reactors as well.
“These customers are basically asking for more capacity, not just energy,” he said. “Our real value add is how to integrate everything for them and try to provide the reliability that they need.”

Storage is also a major focus. According to an August fact sheet, the company had just over a gigawatt of batteries under construction, or nearly 30% of its total capacity under construction, largely in Chile. Meanwhile, AES and Siemens jointly formed the battery maker Fluence in 2018, though that company is now facing grid connection and automation problems.
articles.lede: As demand surges, FERC has approved the IPP and utility company’s take-private deal with BlackRock and EQT.

articles.title: Trump EPA keeps trying to kill Solar for All despite court losses
articles.description: Even a handful of Republicans are questioning the EPA’s repeated attempts to axe the grant program, which would slash energy bills for low-income…
paragraphs: The Trump administration on Tuesday appealed a court ruling that sought to restore the low-income solar program, sparking criticism from not only the typical clean energy proponents but a coalition of Republican allies, too.

The novel program was first envisioned in 2022 as part of the Inflation Reduction Act, with the EPA in 2024 picking winners who’d split a $ 7 billion pot to bolster solar power access for low-income and disadvantaged households. States, local governments, territories, tribes, and nonprofits all got a piece of the pie, and were developing plans to build community solar, rooftop solar, and battery storage when the program first came under attack.

In August 2025, the EPA announced it was killing Solar for All — one of many blows in the Trump administration’s attempt to tear down the Inflation Reduction Act. Advocates, solar installers, and a labor group challenged the decision in court and secured a major victory this September as a federal judge ruled the EPA’s rollback was illegal and that its reasoning for terminating the program was unjustified. A second judge ruled in favor of protecting Solar for All not long after. Some lawsuits seeking to recoup individual grants remain ongoing.

Still, the EPA never resumed grant handouts, and this week, it formally appealed the first of those rulings. Clean energy advocates immediately pushed back, saying that the Trump administration’s continued crusade against Solar for All doesn’t track with its promises to curb power prices.

“ Instead of getting out of the way of a program that will lower energy bills, the Trump administration is continuing its obstruction and delay,” Adam Kent, senior director for green finance at the Natural Resources Defense Council, said in a statement.
A group of six Republican Congress members made a similar case in a letter they sent EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin this week.

“ At a time when energy costs are rising across the country, Solar for All is capable of quickly providing meaningful relief to Americans,” wrote the representatives from Guam, New Jersey, New York, and Pennsylvania. ​ “ We respectfully urge EPA to swiftly reinstate the Solar for All program and ensure projects move forward to implementation as planned.”

The letter is highly unlikely to change the Trump administration’s mind, especially since four of its six signatories will be replaced by Democrats in the next Congress. And slim Republican support aside, the administration doesn’t have a reputation for backing down from its many fights against clean energy.
The U.S. Senate voted Thursday to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, a bill aimed at speeding up energy project permitting.

The final vote to advance the bill was 62 - 33, with Republicans almost unanimously voting in its favor. Fewer Democrats meanwhile voted for the bill’s final passage than elected to bring it to the Senate floor last week. Two Democratic senators authored the bill alongside two Republicans, but many Democrats and climate advocates are worried about how it will benefit fossil fuel projects alongside clean energy. Democrats also voiced concerns that the bill would weaken tribes’ input on energy projects that impact their land.
articles.lede: The Trump administration on Tuesday appealed a court ruling that sought to restore the low-income solar program, sparking criticism from not only the typical clean energy proponents but a coalition of Republican allies, too.

New York awards ports $230M in repurposed offshore wind grants
articles.description: The state planned to invest big in port infrastructure for offshore wind. Amid tough times for the sector, it’s using the funding to serve multiple…
paragraphs: New York state is upgrading its ports for what it hopes will be a return to U.S. offshore wind development in the years after President Donald Trump leaves office.

On Friday, Gov. Kathy Hochul (D) announced over $ 228 million in state funding for five projects to bolster maritime infrastructure along New York’s rivers and harbors, Canary Media is first to report. The investments will enable companies and port operators to expand cargo-handling capacity, add heavy-lift equipment, and boost manufacturing capabilities — all things that could help offshore wind but aren’t limited to that.

The projects ​ “ will make our state prepared to support offshore wind in the future, but it also will ensure the investments produce jobs and economic benefits in the near term,” Doreen Harris, president and CEO of the New York State Energy Research Development Authority, said in an interview.

“ Port facilities and their upgrades tend to be capital-intensive, they tend to have long lead times. So our investments today are long-term in nature,” Harris said. She called the projects ​ “ strong infrastructure development for the state of New York, irrespective of their final use.”

The five awards draw from $ 200 million in grant funding that was initially earmarked to support offshore wind manufacturing and logistics but has been repurposed for maritime infrastructure more broadly. The money all stems from a $ 500 million initiative that Hochul announced for offshore wind in 2022, during a far more optimistic time for the now-beleaguered industry.

In 2019, New York set a target of building 9 gigawatts of offshore wind capacity by 2035 — enough to power roughly 6 million homes — to help meet its larger efforts to decarbonize the state’s electricity sector. As part of that push, state leaders sought to transform ports into job-creating hubs for making, assembling, and servicing the turbines that would spin in the Atlantic Ocean.

NYSERDA provisionally awarded $ 300 million in grant funding to GE Vernova and its subsidiary LM Wind Power in late 2023 to produce offshore wind turbine parts at the Port of Coeymans, along the Hudson River. At the nearby Port of Albany, local authorities began planning a $ 600 million facility that would supply steel tower pieces for offshore wind turbines.

Neither of those projects came to fruition, owing to economic headwinds and a series of supply chain problems, all of which were exacerbated by Trump’s return to the White House in January 2025. Since then, his administration has made continual attempts to halt construction of in-progress wind farms, rescind approvals for planned projects, and thwart prospects for new development.

New York has led the legal fight against many of those actions — including Trump’s stop-work orders for the New York–based Sunrise Wind and Empire Wind projects, which have resumed construction — and the federal government’s unusual strategy of paying offshore wind developers to abandon their leases.

Still, state officials acknowledge that damage has been done to the state’s project pipeline. It is now ​ “ increasingly unlikely” that New York will meet its 9 -GW target in the next decade, owing to the ​ “ significant federal policy uncertainty” around offshore wind, according to the state’s 2025 energy plan.
articles.lede: New York state is upgrading its ports for what it hopes will be a return to U.S. offshore wind development in the years after President Donald Trump leaves office.
